requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: 9to1 MUST apply a platform-wide Privacy Ceiling baseline to every app, framework, cloud service, hosted component, telemetry path, AI feature and operating-system integration that processes personal information. Product teams MUST NOT treat privacy as an app-specific optional enhancement.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: The Privacy Ceiling is derived from the strongest compatible protection required across the supported United States jurisdictions, the United Kingdom and the European Union/EEA, plus deliberate engineering headroom. The implementation MUST maintain a versioned LegalPrivacyProfile describing the currently applicable statutory/regulatory requirements for each supported jurisdiction. Where multiple requirements are compatible, the most protective requirement becomes the global default. Where applicable laws genuinely conflict, the exception MUST be narrowly jurisdiction-scoped, documented, legally reviewed and MUST NOT lower protection for unaffected users or data.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Engineering headroom means 9to1 SHOULD collect less data, retain it for less time, expose it to fewer systems, process it locally more often and encrypt it more comprehensively than the minimum legally permissible where doing so does not prevent the requested product function. A legal maximum retention period, collection scope or disclosure permission MUST NOT automatically become the product default.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Privacy by design and by default is mandatory throughout the product lifecycle. Every processing activity MUST have a declared purpose, lawful/authorised basis where required, data categories, data subjects, recipients/processors, locality/residency constraints where applicable, retention/deletion policy, access-control model and security classification. New processing purposes MUST NOT silently reuse personal data collected for an unrelated purpose merely because the data is technically available.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Data minimisation is mandatory. A component MUST request, collect, transmit, persist and expose only the personal data necessary for its declared purpose and current authorised scope. Optional analytics, diagnostics, personalisation, AI context and convenience features MUST NOT enlarge the mandatory data footprint of the core product without a separate valid basis and user/admin control where required.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Privacy-protective defaults MUST be the ordinary out-of-box state. Settings that materially broaden sharing, retention, discoverability, telemetry, cloud processing, contactability or third-party disclosure MUST be explicit and understandable. Consent or approval surfaces MUST NOT use dark patterns, misleading symmetry, preselected optional consent or unnecessarily difficult withdrawal.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: High-risk processing MUST undergo an appropriate documented privacy/risk assessment before release and again after material architectural or purpose changes. The assessment MUST address foreseeable misuse, unauthorised disclosure, inference risk, vulnerable users, children where relevant, cross-border processing, AI/model exposure, account compromise, metadata leakage and recovery/incident handling.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Encryption MUST be applied in transit and at rest for sensitive personal information unless a documented technical reason makes a specific layer impossible. Where the product promises end-to-end encryption, only intended endpoint participants may possess the content-decryption capability under the declared trust model. A server-side copy of a universal decryption key, silent escrow path or moderation backdoor is incompatible with an E2EE claim unless the user-facing product explicitly describes a materially different encryption model.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: E2EE protects content but does not automatically hide all metadata. 9to1 MUST separately minimise and protect metadata such as participant identifiers, relationship graphs, IP/network information, timestamps, device identifiers, routing information and notification data. User interfaces and documentation MUST NOT imply that metadata is cryptographically hidden when the transport/service necessarily observes it.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: When a feature can use either a local or cloud model/service, the privacy boundary MUST be explicit. Private content MUST NOT leave the device merely because a cloud provider is configured as a model fallback. Uploading personal content to a cloud model/service requires an applicable authorised route, and the UI MUST make materially relevant remote processing understandable to the user.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Secrets, authentication tokens, cryptographic keys and recovery material MUST use dedicated secure storage and least-privilege access. Logs, crash reports, analytics and Action Graph/FullLog data MUST redact secrets and unnecessary personal content rather than creating secondary plaintext stores.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Retention MUST be purpose-bound and enforceable. Personal data MUST have a defined deletion/expiry policy or a documented reason for durable retention. Deletion MUST propagate to replicas, caches, indexes and derived stores according to their declared lifecycle rather than only hiding the primary UI record. Legally required preservation or an explicitly created safety/evidence record MUST be segregated from ordinary user-visible retention and governed by its own scope and expiry rules.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline

These controls SHOULD be easier and more complete than the legal minimum when technically reasonable. Export MUST use interoperable formats where practical and MUST NOT require the user to manually reconstruct data from screenshots or unrelated pages.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: 9to1 MUST maintain an inspectable data-flow inventory and processor/subprocessor register for hosted services. Third parties receive only the scopes/data required for their declared role. A provider's terms permitting additional processing do not by themselves authorise 9to1 to send data for that additional purpose.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Telemetry and product analytics MUST be purpose-limited, minimised and separated from message/document content unless that content is genuinely required for a specifically disclosed diagnostic purpose. Sensitive content MUST NOT be collected merely to improve general analytics. Privacy-preserving aggregation/pseudonymisation SHOULD be used where it meaningfully reduces risk.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Security/privacy failures MUST fail closed where continuing would expose personal content or silently weaken a promised protection. If an encryption, permission, privacy-relay or policy control required for a sensitive operation is unavailable, the operation MUST stop or visibly degrade to a clearly described lower-protection mode only when the user is allowed to choose that mode.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline

Any exception to the Privacy Ceiling MUST identify the exact requirement, jurisdiction/product scope, necessity, user impact, data affected, compensating controls, approval authority and review/expiry date.

requirements.heading: Privacy and data-protection baseline
requirements.requirement: Privacy acceptance MUST include automated and manual tests for least-privilege access, unauthorised cross-app data access, cloud/local boundary enforcement, retention/deletion propagation, export correctness, consent/withdrawal, encryption-state truthfulness, metadata minimisation, log redaction, provider failure and jurisdiction-profile changes. requirements.requirement: Every 9to1 app must expose a first-party automation API whose action surface is exhaustive for user-accessible app functionality. An authorised MCP, plugin, script, agent or other client must be able to perform anything the user can perform in the app through supported UI, subject to the same account, object, platform and security restrictions. requirements.heading: Acceptance criteria
requirements.requirement: Any implementation that recreates CUI as an AXAML preprocessor, uses polling for ordinary live variables, treats Hidden as unloaded, treats Active as destructive property reset, mutates underlying elements through Background backdrop modifiers, snapshots Blur/Refract instead of keeping them live, silently guesses ambiguous shorthand, partially applies incompatible Group mutations, or exposes unreviewed donor/property capability gaps MUST fail release conformance.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Home runtime dependency
requirements.requirement: Every installable/native 9to1 app has a hard runtime dependency on 9-1 Home. Before initialising the app’s normal UI or opening user artifacts, the app MUST complete a local Home availability/version handshake against the Home-managed shared services it requires.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Home runtime dependency
requirements.requirement: If Home is not installed, the app MUST refuse normal startup and display only a minimal bootstrap surface explaining that 9-1 Home is required. The bootstrap surface MUST provide an Install Home action that opens/starts the trusted Home installation flow. It MUST NOT create or mutate normal app data while Home is absent.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Home runtime dependency
requirements.requirement: If Home is installed but the required shared service/API version is missing, incompatible or damaged, the app MUST refuse unsafe normal startup and offer the appropriate Home update/repair flow with a structured reason. Apps MUST NOT silently launch private replacement services to bypass the missing Home dependency.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: Every interactive 9to1 app MUST expose the shared persistent floating contextual AI bar at the bottom of its primary content surface. The bar uses Dulche plus the owning app's authorised semantic state. It MUST be able to inspect the current artifact/surface semantically and, when permitted, edit it through the owning app's typed APIs. The bar is not limited to whatever pixels happen to be visible in the viewport.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: The shared bar MUST expose an explicit persistent AI access-mode switcher with at least Read-only and Write mode. The current mode MUST remain visible enough that the user can tell whether Dulche may only inspect the surface or may also request mutations. This switcher is a platform-wide interaction contract used consistently by Write, Present, Boards, Files, Canvas, Data, Mail, Planner and every other surface that hosts the shared bar.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: In Read-only mode, Dulche MAY read, search, compare, reason over, summarise, explain and navigate the full authorised semantic surface, including off-screen content that the owning app exposes. It MAY generate proposed changes in conversation, but MUST NOT mutate the owning artifact, structure or app state. Read-only access does not imply permission to inspect data outside the caller's normal authorisation boundary.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: In Write mode, Dulche receives the same semantic read context plus the owning app's permitted typed mutation actions. Write mode is capability to request/perform edits, not permission to bypass app state, trust, confirmation, review, external-side-effect or security rules. Mutations MUST use stable semantic identities such as ArtifactID, PageID, SectionID, ObjectID, row/range/entity IDs or equivalent domain identifiers and the owning app's normal revision/conflict semantics.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: Apps MUST provide a permission-filtered semantic context snapshot including the active artifact/page/entity, current selection, relevant stable object IDs, structure necessary to understand the task, current revision/state and supported typed actions. The bar MUST prefer this semantic context over screenshot/OCR/pixel interpretation and MUST NOT substitute raw mouse/keyboard/desktop automation when typed context/actions exist.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: The AI bar MUST remain visually separate from document/page content and MUST NOT change the underlying artifact layout merely by being shown. It MAY collapse to a compact state but MUST remain directly reachable without navigating to a separate AI page. Read/Write mode changes the AI's effective capability only; it does not create a second copy of the current artifact.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: Surface-specific mutation protections MAY be stricter than the shared Write-mode baseline and cannot be weakened by AI mode or trust state. Data is the mandatory example: every AI-requested Data mutation requires explicit approval for that specific action even while the bar is in Write mode. When the target is a live database, Data MUST additionally show a meaningful preview/diff, validate the operation and create a recoverable backup/snapshot/checkpoint before execution. If the required live-database backup cannot be created, the mutation MUST NOT proceed as though rollback exists.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: For Data live-database changes, the approval surface SHOULD identify the intended operation, affected tables/entities/rows where knowable, schema/dependency impact, external side effects and backup identity. Execution MUST occur only after approval, then verify the actual result and preserve rollback/recovery information. Prior approval, Accept and Trust or Always Trust MUST NOT suppress this Data-specific per-action approval invariant.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: Equivalent bar actions MUST behave consistently across product surfaces, while menus and available operations remain context-sensitive to the owning app. Unsupported or inapplicable actions MUST not be exposed merely to make the bar look feature-complete.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Chat bar — expanded-mode formatting and emoji controls
requirements.requirement: Visibility and placement: Show the following buttons inline next to the plus (+) button only when the chat bar is both focused and in its expanded composer layout, with the text-entry area above the bottom controls. These buttons must not appear in compact/mini mode, even when the compact/mini chat bar is focused.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Chat-bar control acceptance
requirements.requirement: Verify that Aa and the emoji button appear beside + only while the expanded composer is focused; neither appears in compact/mini mode. The formatting toolbar and CUI emoji picker MUST work with keyboard input, labelled controls, focus return and preserved draft/selection state.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.requirement: Every interactive 9to1 app that hosts the shared persistent AI bar MUST use Home's canonical compose invocation component and cross-app dispatcher. Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents, Files and the reserved @Computer Use capability MUST therefore resolve consistently across apps rather than each product implementing a private @ syntax or resource picker.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.requirement: When a target 9to1 app owns the requested artifact/action, the originating model MUST use the target app's typed API/shared semantic action contract and MAY ask Home to launch/reveal the target app so the user can observe progress. For example, a request to create a presentation routes to Present and creates/edits a canonical Present artifact rather than fabricating a slide-like object in the originating app.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.requirement: Computer Use MUST NOT be selected automatically as a fallback when typed app execution is unavailable, inconvenient or fails. It is usable only after explicit @Computer Use invocation and remains subject to the Computer Use eligibility, permission, game-exclusion and Autoreview rules.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.requirement: Model-driven typed edits MAY be visualised in the target app with live object motion, selection highlights, text insertion and a synthetic/virtual cursor. This visualisation is not evidence that Dulche is literally controlling the pointer; the typed action/result remains authoritative and the synthetic cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's actual input cursor.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Launch Screens

If a capability is not applicable, the product section MUST explicitly state the exclusion and reason rather than silently omit it:
