requirements.heading: Launch Screens
requirements.requirement: The launch screen must use CUI and the app’s real storage/project model. Recent, favourite, shared and template entries must be functional data-backed surfaces rather than static mock content. Apps may add app-specific quick actions, onboarding/tours or account/storage indicators where useful.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Launch Screens
requirements.requirement: The following apps must include a launch/home screen:
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Web Apps
requirements.requirement: Cakemods.com MUST host a web version of every 9-1 Workspace/AI product that is not explicitly listed as web-exempt. Web surfaces MUST share the same CAKE ID identity, canonical artifact formats, domain APIs, permission model and underlying server-side entities as desktop equivalents. Browser-specific UI/layout MAY differ, but it MUST NOT create a separate incompatible product model.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Web Apps
requirements.requirement: Web exemption is permitted only when the product’s core function requires infrastructure, privileged device access or hosted compute that CAKE does not currently provide. Each exemption MUST state the blocking capability/infrastructure. Exemptions MUST be re-evaluated when that blocker is removed; exemption is not a permanent product classification.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Product role and ownership
requirements.requirement: 9-1 Home is the mandatory native ecosystem hub, platform shell and control plane for installed 9to1 applications. It is not merely a dashboard application. Home owns shared platform services that must have one canonical implementation across the ecosystem: app/package management, the Home Core service registry, shared Dulche lifecycle/broker coordination, permission/trust brokerage, account/subscription state, the Shared Productivity Engine, shared model/provider configuration, Action Graph rendering, Mesh coordination, notifications, shared search/index coordination and ecosystem-wide settings.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Product role and ownership
requirements.requirement: Other apps MUST consume Home-owned shared services through supported authenticated interfaces and MUST NOT silently launch incompatible private replacements when a Home service is unavailable. App-owned documents, projects and domain data remain owned by their respective apps/storage layers; Home MUST NOT become the only canonical copy of another app’s artifacts.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Product role and ownership
requirements.requirement: Home installation includes the Home Core background service/runtime required by native apps plus the Home user-facing CUI shell. Native apps require a compatible Home installation/Home Core service, but the visible Home window does not need to remain open while other apps run. On 9to1-OS, Home Core may be integrated as a system component while preserving the same service contracts.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Home shell and navigation
requirements.requirement: The Home shell MUST be dashboard/home-oriented rather than primarily a conventional settings application. Its stable primary navigation MUST provide at least Home/Dashboard, Apps, Library, Events, Discover, Mesh and Settings. Account/profile controls MAY live in persistent shell chrome. Chat remains a Spaces destination and MUST NOT become Home’s primary landing surface.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Home shell and navigation
requirements.requirement: Navigation destinations MUST preserve their own scroll/filter/selection state while the Home process remains active where practical. Deep links from notifications, Go, other apps or the OS MUST be able to open the relevant Home destination/object directly without first routing through the Dashboard.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: The 9-1 AI Dashboard is a generative briefing/dashboard surface, not a chat landing page. It MUST assemble permission-authorised cross-app information into a concise live brief and MUST derive every surfaced tile from identifiable source entities/events or an explicitly generated synthesis over identifiable sources.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: Dashboard tiles MAY surface upcoming Planner items, tasks, recent files/artifacts, project progress, reminders, travel/routes, Agent or Automation status, relevant Mail/messages, package/update state, storage/account warnings and other timely ecosystem context. Every actionable tile MUST use typed app actions; the Dashboard MUST NOT use raw UI automation to perform app mutations.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: Dashboard layout is user-configurable. The user MUST be able to add supported fixed/provider tiles, remove/hide tiles, resize tiles where the tile declares supported sizes, drag/reorder tiles, arrange tiles into the supported responsive layout, pin/lock tiles against automated movement and restore/reset a layout.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: The canonical DashboardLayout MUST use stable TileInstanceID values and store at least TileType, source/provider identity, position/order, declared size, user visibility state, pinned/locked state, tile-specific configuration and layout revision. Responsive rendering MAY adapt exact pixel/grid placement to the current window/device, but it MUST preserve the user’s semantic ordering/grouping and pinned constraints.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: Manual user layout changes are authoritative. Automated generation/reordering MUST NOT silently overwrite a newer manual layout revision. When a layout conflict occurs across synced devices, Home MUST preserve both revisions or resolve through an explicit revision/merge policy rather than blind last-write-wins.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: Dashboard settings MUST expose two independent user controls: AllowAIGeneratedTiles and AllowAIReorder. These controls are opt-in/opt-out independently; disabling one MUST NOT implicitly disable the other.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: When AllowAIGeneratedTiles = false, Dulche/Generative UI MUST NOT create new arbitrary Dashboard tile instances. Existing user-added/system/provider tiles remain usable, and AI MAY still generate content inside a tile whose explicit tile contract permits generated content.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: When AllowAIGeneratedTiles = true, Dulche MAY create contextually useful temporary or persisted tiles through the safe Generative UI/CUI schema. Generated tiles MUST declare provenance, the source entities/events they summarise, their lifetime/persistence policy and available typed actions. Generated tiles MUST NOT inject arbitrary executable code.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: When AllowAIReorder = false, Dulche MUST NOT move, resize, regroup, reorder or hide existing tiles. When AllowAIReorder = true, Dulche MAY optimise unpinned/unlocked tile placement according to user goals/context, but MUST NOT move or resize tiles marked pinned/locked, MUST preserve explicit hidden-tile choices, and MUST retain an undoable prior layout revision.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: AI layout changes MUST be attributable in Events/audit history and MUST be reversible. A user action that manually repositions or pins a tile immediately supersedes older AI layout intent for that tile.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: Apps and Home services MAY register Dashboard tile providers through a versioned provider contract. A provider MUST declare TileType, source app/service, supported sizes, required permissions, refresh policy, data dependencies, available actions, whether the tile can be instantiated manually, and whether its content may be generated/modified by Dulche.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dashboard
requirements.requirement: Tile data MUST remain source-backed. A tile provider that loses access to its source MUST enter an unavailable/stale state with an explanation rather than silently displaying fabricated current data. Permission revocation MUST prevent future refresh/access and purge or redact cached sensitive content according to the owning source’s policy.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Apps surface and package management
requirements.requirement: Home Apps is the primary native app catalogue and management surface. It MUST show installed and available 9to1 apps/packages with stable PackageID/AppID, name/icon, installed version, available version, update channel, installation state, dependency/compatibility state, update availability and repair/rollback availability where supported.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Apps surface and package management
requirements.requirement: Home MUST support install, uninstall, update, repair, launch/open, channel/version selection where allowed and rollback to a validated previous package version where retained. Uninstalling an app MUST NOT silently delete user-created artifacts owned by that app. Artifact-retention/deletion MUST be a separate explicit operation governed by the owning app/storage semantics.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Apps surface and package management
requirements.requirement: Package installation/update MUST use staged validation and atomic activation. Integrity/signature verification, dependency resolution and Home/shared-service compatibility checks MUST complete before activation. A failed activation MUST leave the previous known-good package usable when rollback data is available.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Apps surface and package management
requirements.requirement: Home and Launcher MUST consume one canonical package/update database and service. Launcher is the bootstrap/outside-Home client of the same package system; it MUST NOT maintain a second incompatible installer/updater state.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Library
requirements.requirement: Library is Home’s cross-app artifact index/browser, not a duplicate Files app and not a separate storage authority. It MUST surface canonical references to authorised artifacts across 9to1 apps, including recent, favourite/pinned, shared, generated/created and app/type-filtered content where applicable.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Library
requirements.requirement: Every Library entry MUST identify the canonical owning app, stable artifact/entity ID, display name, artifact type, relevant location/owner/share metadata and last-modified state. Opening a Library item routes to the owning app/surface and MUST NOT create a duplicate artifact merely because the item is listed in Home.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Library
requirements.requirement: Library search/filter/sort MUST use the shared search/index service but enforce current permissions at query/open time. Revoked or deleted artifacts MUST not remain usable through stale Library entries.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Events
requirements.requirement: Events is Home’s ecosystem activity/timeline surface. It is not Planner’s calendar. Events MUST aggregate authorised typed activity from apps/services such as Agent/Automation runs, package/update events, permission/trust decisions, important artifact changes, Mesh/device events, notifications and other meaningful system activity.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Events
requirements.requirement: Each Event MUST have a stable EventID, timestamp, source app/service, event type, actor/caller identity where relevant, object/entity references, severity/category, human-readable summary and typed deep-link/action references where available. Events MAY reference RequestID/ActionGraphID for AI/agentic activity.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Events
requirements.requirement: Events MUST preserve source provenance and MUST NOT invent event history from generated summaries. Home MAY generate a concise natural-language digest of events, but the underlying event records remain the authority.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Discover
requirements.requirement: 9-1 Discover is the model browser/discovery surface inside Home. It MUST aggregate model/catalogue information from configured providers rather than depend on one catalogue. Search, filter and comparison MUST support model identity, provider/origin, modality, capabilities, architecture/parameter information when known, context limits, quantisation/format where known, local/cloud status, hardware-fit estimate, install/connection state, entitlement/cost class and privacy/residency information.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Discover
requirements.requirement: Discover MUST treat Chat, Image and Voice as first-class model categories. Advanced discovery additionally exposes Audio and Video models. Voice MUST NOT be buried under Audio: conversational/live voice is a primary model category because it has distinct runtime, quality and capability requirements.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Discover
requirements.requirement: Voice discovery MUST expose capability metadata such as Conversational compatibility, Monologue compatibility, Live Listener compatibility, Live Translate compatibility, visual understanding, tool/action support, streaming, interruption/turn-taking support, supported languages/accents and translation language pairs when known, one-way/bidirectional/multi-language live interpretation support, local/cloud execution, latency characteristics, privacy/residency and entitlement/cost.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Discover
requirements.requirement: Discover MUST recommend the highest-quality compatible Voice models/configurations for the user's required mode and constraints. Recommendation dimensions MAY include reasoning quality, speech naturalness, speech-recognition accuracy, expressiveness, instruction following, turn-taking quality, interruption handling, long-form coherence, audio-context understanding, visual capability, tool reliability and latency. Unknown measurements remain Unknown rather than being invented.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Discover
requirements.requirement: Voice recommendations MUST be contextual rather than a single universal ranking. Discover may surface labels such as Highest quality, Best for Conversational, Best for Monologue, Best for Live Listener, Best for Live Translate, Best local and Fastest when supported by actual capability/evaluation data. Each recommendation MUST explain the relevant reasons/constraints rather than presenting an unexplained badge. Live Translate recommendations should consider speech-recognition accuracy, translation quality, output-speech quality, latency, turn detection, code-switching and multi-language support where measured.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Discover
requirements.requirement: Discover MAY recommend either a native realtime Voice Model or, where 9to1 supports it, a compatible composite voice configuration. Composite implementation detail is secondary to the normal user-facing Voice selection and MUST NOT force ordinary users to manually assemble STT/reasoning/TTS pipelines.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Discover
requirements.requirement: When a selected Voice Model exposes multiple named voices, Discover MUST show those voices as selectable variants with the underlying Voice Model as secondary metadata. Voice-quality/model recommendations and named-voice selection are distinct concepts.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Discover
requirements.requirement: A model listing MUST preserve stable provider-scoped identity even when multiple providers expose the same human-readable model name. Unknown metadata MUST remain unknown rather than being fabricated.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Discover
requirements.requirement: Discover MUST support the relevant install/pull/connect/open-in-picker action for providers that expose those capabilities. Install/connect actions route through Dulche/provider/package APIs and the normal permission/account model.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Universal Model Picker
requirements.requirement: The Universal Model Picker is the single shared model/provider selection and routing interface for the 9to1 ecosystem. On Windows/regular 9to1 it is hosted by Home; on 9to1-OS the same canonical state is surfaced by the OS. Apps, Agents and AI surfaces MUST NOT create incompatible private model pickers, provider registries or fallback logic when this shared capability applies.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Simple defaults and capability categories
requirements.requirement: Image supports an explicit Inherit from Active/Chat route. Inheritance means use that ordered route and its native image-generation/editing-capable candidates; it MUST NOT silently substitute an unrelated unconfigured image provider. A dedicated Image route is an explicit override.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Active and Background routes
requirements.requirement: If no Background route is configured, background work inherits the Active route subject to normal capability/privacy/policy filtering. A task-specific explicit model outranks Agent/app/category defaults; a configured Background route applies only to eligible background work and MUST NOT override an explicit Agent/task requirement.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Ordered Model Routes
requirements.requirement: Home/Dulche MUST support versioned ordered Model Routes shared by regular 9to1 and 9to1-OS. A Model Route is an ordered list of stable configured model identities plus per-entry enabled/disabled state and routing policy. Users can reorder candidates directly in Home, including by drag/reorder UI, without changing the models' canonical identities.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Ordered Model Routes
requirements.requirement: Example: an Active route may be ChatGPT 6 Sol → Gemma 4 → Fable 5. The ordering means use the highest-priority candidate that is both eligible and available for the request. The router MUST evaluate compatibility before invocation rather than deliberately sending impossible requests to higher entries first.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Eligibility-first routing
requirements.requirement: After filtering, Dulche selects the highest-priority available candidate. A lower candidate may be used automatically when a higher candidate is unavailable because of a classified routing condition such as usage/quota exhaustion, provider/model outage, unsupported required capability, context incompatibility, authentication/provider unavailability when another authorised option exists, or local resource insufficiency after permitted reclamation.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Eligibility-first routing
requirements.requirement: Capability mismatch should normally be detected before invocation. For example, if the first two models in a route cannot generate video and the third can, a video-generation request routes directly to the third eligible model rather than failing through the first two.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Conditions that are not model fallback
requirements.requirement: Model fallback is not a generic retry mechanism. Errors such as missing user files, invalid tool arguments, target-app permission denial, required human approval, business-logic rejection or an external service action failure do not justify silently switching models unless the failure is independently classified as a model/provider-routing condition.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Fallback privacy and control
requirements.requirement: A request explicitly pinned to a model with fallback disabled MUST fail transparently rather than silently substitute another model. Likewise a local-only request cannot fall through to cloud merely because the local model is unavailable.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Selection inheritance and overrides
requirements.requirement: The configuration hierarchy MUST be deterministic: request-specific explicit selection → Agent/task override → app/surface override → capability/category route → Background route for eligible background work or Active route for foreground work → configured route fallbacks. A lower-level explicit override wins, while inherited state is visibly distinguishable from an explicit override.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Reasoning and capability validation
requirements.requirement: The picker renders only reasoning/effort levels actually exposed by the selected model/provider. It MUST NOT invent Low/Medium/High controls for a model that does not support them. Incompatible explicit selections are blocked or clearly explained unless an authorised fallback route can satisfy the requirement.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
requirements.requirement: Regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use one canonical Dulche model catalogue and versioned routing contract.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
requirements.requirement: Users can use one Active Model for everything compatible or configure separate capability/app/Agent and Background routes.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
requirements.requirement: Ordered model routing automatically falls through on classified quota, availability, capability, context or resource conditions while respecting privacy, permissions and admin policy.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
requirements.requirement: Capability mismatch is filtered before invocation where knowable; model fallback is not misused for unrelated tool/app/business-logic failures.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
requirements.requirement: Users can reorder, enable/disable and inspect route candidates and understand which model ultimately handled a request.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
requirements.requirement: Voice named variants, Image inheritance, Advanced Audio/Video, reasoning controls, aliases and local-model lifecycle preserve the existing category-specific contracts.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dulche runtime control
requirements.requirement: Home Core owns the single shared Dulche broker/runtime lifecycle for native 9to1 apps. It MAY host multiple logical endpoints/models concurrently subject to resource policy, but apps MUST attach to the shared broker rather than launching competing private model servers.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dulche runtime control
requirements.requirement: Home MUST expose shared Dulche service state including Starting, Ready, Degraded, Restarting and Stopped plus endpoint/model load state, resource pressure and health/diagnostic information required for recovery. Logical EndpointID/SessionID identity remains governed by the Dulche Runtime contract.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Dulche runtime control
requirements.requirement: If the visible Home shell closes, Home Core MAY continue in the background. If Home Core crashes/restarts, attached apps MUST enter a degraded/reconnecting state for Home-dependent features, preserve their own user data, and reconnect to restored shared services. Apps MUST NOT launch private replacement Dulche servers during recovery.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Permission and trust broker
requirements.requirement: Settings MUST expose a Permissions & Trust management surface where the user can inspect caller identity/origin, granted apps/actions/scopes, trust level, creation/expiry, last-use metadata where available, and revoke/block/unblock/narrow grants. Revocation MUST affect future actions immediately subject to in-flight action semantics defined by the target API.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Mesh
requirements.requirement: Every Mesh device MUST have a stable DeviceID bound to an authenticated device identity/key rather than a mutable device name. Pairing MUST require explicit user/account authorisation and establish an authenticated encrypted relationship. A device advertises supported 9to1 capabilities/services and versions; peers MUST NOT assume capabilities that were not advertised.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Mesh
requirements.requirement: Mesh data sharing/sync MUST be namespace/object scoped. Personal Mesh may sync selected personal Den/chat/context/project state; Team/Organisation modes may sync explicitly shared team/org state while preserving personal/private namespaces. Joining Mesh MUST NOT automatically share all local files, secrets, model context or app data.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Mesh
requirements.requirement: Remote capability invocation MUST use typed APIs and pass both caller-side and target-device permission/policy checks. Mesh MUST NOT become an implicit generic remote-desktop, mouse/keyboard or arbitrary-code-execution channel.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Mesh
requirements.requirement: Lost/revoked devices MUST be removable from Home. Revocation invalidates future Mesh authentication/session material for that device and prevents further sync/remote calls. Offline devices queue only operations whose owning service explicitly supports safe offline replay/conflict handling.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Action Graph renderer
requirements.requirement: Any authorised app MAY host the shared renderer given an authorised RequestID/ActionGraphID. Home MUST NOT create a second execution history or mutate Dulche’s causal graph merely for presentation. Events, Agents, Spaces and other surfaces MAY deep-link into the same renderer.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: Home owns the reusable base component/service contract for the global persistent bottom AI bar required by interactive 9to1 apps. The shared component provides CUI rendering, Dulche connection, Universal Model Picker integration, permission/trust plumbing, request state and common Action Graph access.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.requirement: Each host app MUST provide the bar with a permission-filtered semantic context snapshot and its typed supported actions. Home MUST NOT obtain app context through raw screen scraping when the host provides structured context. App-specific mutation semantics remain owned by the target app APIs.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.requirement: The shared Home-owned floating AI compose component MUST provide one searchable @ invocation menu for Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents and Files. The menu is a single interaction surface with collapsible type sections rather than separate unrelated pickers. Typing @ opens the resource list; typing text after @ filters across all sections while preserving each result's type and identity.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.requirement: Selecting an item inserts an inline invocation chip/token inside the compose field at the caret position. The rendered token MUST display the resource's icon where available plus its human-readable label, for example an Agent may render as '@[agent icon] John'. The token MUST use a distinct invoked visual state, including colour/style differentiation, while also using non-colour cues for accessibility. Editing/deleting the token removes or changes the invocation rather than leaving invisible hidden attachment state.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.requirement: Invocation tokens MUST store stable canonical identities, not only display text: Plugin PackageID/version or resolved active version, SkillID/version, AppID, AgentID/DefinitionRevision where required and File/Artifact reference identity/revision or access token as appropriate. Duplicate display names MUST therefore remain unambiguous. The resolved invocation set is included in request metadata, FullLog and Action Graph.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.requirement: The Apps section MUST contain every installed/available first-party 9to1 app plus user-installed applications that 9to1 can classify as safely operable through a typed API/integration or, when separately authorised, Computer Use. App entries MUST expose whether their interaction path is Typed/API, Computer Use Required, or both. Selecting an app whose only route is Computer Use MUST NOT activate Computer Use by itself; the request also requires the explicit @Computer Use invocation.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.requirement: Game executables and anti-cheat-protected game surfaces MUST be excluded from the operable Apps invocation results even when discovered through Steam, Epic Games Launcher or another launcher/library. If 9to1 cannot confidently distinguish an eligible ordinary application from a game/anti-cheat target, it MUST omit or mark the target unavailable for Computer Use rather than risk automation. Play remains the supported Agent-game route defined by its own contract.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.requirement: @Computer Use is a reserved first-party system capability entry in the same searchable invocation surface. Selecting it creates the explicit ComputerUseInvocationID required by the Dulche Computer Use contract and makes its active state visible in the compose field before the request is submitted.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.requirement: Models operating inside any 9to1 app MAY invoke another 9to1 app only when the user's request explicitly names/invokes that app, directly asks for an outcome owned by that app, or unambiguously implies the owning app from the requested artifact/action. For example, 'create a presentation' resolves to Present; 'make a spreadsheet' resolves to Data; an unrelated app MUST NOT be opened merely because the model thinks it might be useful.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.requirement: Cross-app intent resolution MUST bind to the owning app's stable AppID and typed capability contract. If the required app is not running, Home MAY launch/open it automatically when that is part of fulfilling the request. The target artifact remains canonical in its owning app, and the originating app/Space receives references/status rather than an unmanaged duplicate.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.requirement: Where an app has a visible editing surface, the user SHOULD be able to watch model-driven edits occur in real time. Home/shared app infrastructure MUST provide an execution-visualisation stream that maps semantic actions to visible UI changes such as objects moving, text appearing, selections changing, slides being created or a virtual cursor hovering over the affected target.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.requirement: The execution visualiser is representational, not the control mechanism. A virtual cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's real pointer and MUST NOT generate mouse/keyboard input merely to make the animation believable. The canonical typed API/action result remains authoritative; visual animation follows confirmed/provisional semantic events and MUST reconcile to final app state after errors, retries or rollback.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.requirement: Home Settings MUST expose global conversation presentation preferences for Plain text versus Speech bubbles. The preference applies to compatible 9to1 conversational/AI surfaces through the shared renderer rather than each app inventing a different message layout.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.requirement: User-message alignment and model-message alignment MUST be independently configurable as Left or Right. All four combinations are valid, including both parties on the same side. Alignment changes presentation only and MUST NOT alter message order, authorship, accessibility reading order or exported conversation data.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.requirement: The selected Dulche thinking-log mode (Precise, Concise, Detailed or Ramble) MUST be configurable in the same AI/conversation settings family. Inline thinking/work regions render beneath or between message text according to chronology; when Speech bubbles are enabled, the thinking/work region visually belongs beneath the relevant model bubble without being styled as ordinary model-authored message text.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.requirement: Thinking/work presentation MUST use lower visual emphasis than normal chat while remaining readable and accessible. Collapsed 'Thought for ...'/'Worked for ...', ETA status, blockers and Problem events MUST use the same shared renderer across apps so equivalent Runtime state is not represented differently by each product.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: Home owns the Shared Productivity Engine used by Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces for overlapping document/object behaviours. The engine is a shared canonical object/rendering/action layer, not five copied implementations. App shells MAY provide different workflows and layout chrome, but a shared object type MUST use the same schema, formatting semantics, rendering rules and typed object actions wherever that type is supported.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: The initial required shared object families include rich text/paragraphs, headings, lists/checklists, code blocks, equations, tables, images/media, drawings/ink, graph objects and typed embedded 9to1 artifact references. The registry MUST be extensible so a new shared object type can be implemented once and enabled in multiple supporting surfaces without rewriting its core editor/renderer.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: Every shared object instance MUST have a stable ObjectID within its owning artifact plus a versioned ObjectType/schema identifier. Object content, formatting, accessibility metadata, asset references and app-neutral layout properties MUST be serialisable independently from transient UI state. Unknown required schema versions MUST fail explicitly rather than being silently flattened or reinterpreted.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: Shared object schemas MUST preserve enough information for semantically identical rendering/editing across participating apps. If an app cannot support a property, it MUST retain that property in the object payload when round-tripping and surface the limitation instead of destructively stripping it.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: The engine MUST provide a shared versioned style registry for reusable text/paragraph/object style definitions. Style definitions use stable StyleID identity independent of display name so renaming a style does not detach existing objects. App-specific style extensions MAY exist but MUST preserve shared base properties when transferred.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: The engine MUST provide a versioned ProductivityObjectBundle clipboard/transfer format containing shared object payloads, style definitions, asset references, accessibility metadata and a portable fallback representation. Copying a supported object from one participating app and pasting it into another MUST preserve the same shared-object semantics and appearance rather than converting it to an image or lossy app-specific approximation.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: When the destination supports the same shared object type, paste creates/imports a native shared object instance using the same schema. When the destination does not support that object type but supports embedded 9to1 artifacts, the UI MUST offer an embed/reference path. Destructive flattening is allowed only as an explicit export/paste-as-static action.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: Spaces MUST use the Shared Productivity Engine for rich pasted/embedded content so tables, code blocks, drawings, graphs and other shared objects preserve their structure instead of degrading to plain text. Spaces may present a conversational shell around the object, but editing MUST route through the same shared object actions.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: The engine MUST provide shared selection, focus, formatting, object insertion/removal, resize/transform where applicable, clipboard, accessibility and undoable action primitives for shared object types. Shared actions MUST have stable typed representations so compatible apps can participate in undo/recovery and AI/Automation execution without reproducing hidden per-app commands.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: App-specific shells MAY add contextual commands, but MUST NOT fork the underlying object semantics into incompatible versions. Object actions MUST be exposed through typed APIs and usable by UI, Spaces, Automations and Dulche-driven AI without raw UI simulation.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: The shared engine MUST emit semantic selection/context information for the persistent AI bar and app-specific contextual toolbars. This context MUST contain stable object/selection identity rather than requiring consumers to infer meaning from rendered pixels.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: The shared engine MUST expose the Rnote-derived drawing/ink engine as a reusable shared object/layer so Canvas and Boards use the same stroke model, pen/eraser behaviours and serialisation primitives. Other productivity surfaces MAY opt into the same drawing object without implementing a separate ink stack.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: Home Core MUST expose the Shared Productivity Engine as a versioned shared platform capability. Apps may link/embed approved shared engine libraries/components as part of their package for rendering performance, but the canonical schema registry, compatibility negotiation and shared service/version authority remain Home-owned. Apps MUST validate compatible engine/schema versions during startup.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: Shared object schemas and ProductivityObjectBundle MUST be versioned independently of individual app versions. Home MUST expose compatibility negotiation so an older app can detect a newer unsupported shared object type/property before editing. Compatible unknown optional properties MUST be preserved; incompatible required features MUST produce a structured compatibility state rather than silent data loss.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.requirement: The above are minimum cross-app entry points. Each shared object type MUST also expose its typed creation/update/query actions through the owning app/API surface required by the global API-parity rule.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Settings
requirements.requirement: Home Settings owns ecosystem-wide settings only. The Settings surface MUST include at least Account & Subscription, Appearance/CUI, AI & Models, Permissions & Trust, Apps & Updates, Storage, Mesh & Devices, Privacy, Accessibility, Notifications and Advanced/Diagnostics. App-specific preferences remain in the owning app unless a setting intentionally governs multiple apps.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Settings
requirements.requirement: Settings changes MUST use typed settings keys/schemas with validation and explicit scope (device, account, workspace/team or organisation where applicable). Unknown or incompatible settings versions MUST NOT be silently discarded during upgrade/downgrade.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Account and subscription surface
requirements.requirement: Home MUST provide the primary native CAKE ID account/subscription surface. It displays authenticated user identity, organisation/workspace context where applicable, current configured subscription/preset source, EntitlementPriceMonthly, EffectiveThresholds, EffectiveEntitlements, AI Dust balance/allocation/usage, storage allocation/usage, site limits/usage and active sessions/devices using server-authoritative values.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Account and subscription surface
requirements.requirement: Home MUST NOT recalculate paid entitlements locally from a displayed tier label. Checkout, plan changes and sensitive billing management hand off to the trusted authenticated CAKEMODS billing flow defined by the Accounts & Subscription contract. Sign-out/session revocation actions MUST preserve local user data according to each app’s offline/storage policy rather than deleting it by default.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Notifications
requirements.requirement: Home owns the native 9to1 notification service/centre. Apps publish typed notifications containing NotificationID, source app/service, category/severity, title/body, created time, read/dismissed state, related entity references and typed actions/deep links. Notifications MUST NOT encode consequential behaviour only as arbitrary executable callbacks.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Notifications
requirements.requirement: Home MUST support notification history, read/unread state, dismiss/clear subject to retention policy, per-source/category preferences and deep-link actions. Where Windows/9to1-OS system notifications are available, Home MAY bridge eligible notifications to the OS while retaining the canonical 9to1 notification record/state.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared search and Go indexing
requirements.requirement: Home owns/co-ordinates the shared searchable-entity index consumed by Go and Home Library/Search. Apps MUST publish supported searchable entity metadata through a typed indexing contract rather than Home scraping arbitrary app databases.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared search and Go indexing
requirements.requirement: Search records MUST include stable source app, EntityID/type, title/display metadata, search/index text or vector references as permitted, modification state and current access-scope metadata. Search results MUST re-check current authorisation before exposing sensitive content or opening an entity; stale index access MUST NOT bypass revoked permissions.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Shared search and Go indexing
requirements.requirement: On deletion/revocation, apps MUST be able to invalidate/remove affected index records. Home may maintain rebuildable indexes/caches, but the index MUST NOT become the only canonical copy of source content.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Service registry and compatibility handshake
requirements.requirement: Home Core MUST expose a machine-readable service registry describing Home-owned platform capabilities and versions. At minimum it includes Dulche broker/runtime coordination, permission/trust broker, Shared Productivity Engine, package/update service, notifications, search/index, Mesh and account/session capability availability.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Service registry and compatibility handshake
requirements.requirement: Before normal startup, every native 9to1 app MUST complete a compatibility handshake against Home Core and declare the required service/capability versions it needs. Missing/incompatible required services result in the global Home repair/update/bootstrap flow rather than undefined partial operation.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Service registry and compatibility handshake
requirements.requirement: Service identity/version MUST be explicit; apps MUST NOT infer compatibility solely from the Home marketing version string.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.requirement: Home Core MUST auto-start on demand or at session startup when required by installed 9to1 apps. Closing the visible Home window MUST NOT necessarily stop Home Core. Home Core shutdown is allowed only when no required dependent operation is active or when the user/system explicitly requests full 9to1 service shutdown.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.requirement: Home Core persistent state MUST use crash-safe versioned storage. Corrupt or incompatible Home state MUST enter a diagnosable recovery/repair mode; Home MUST NOT silently discard permission grants, package state, device identities or other durable control-plane state to regain startup.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.requirement: If a Home service fails while apps are open, dependent apps MUST receive a structured service-unavailable/degraded signal. They MUST preserve their own artifact state and block only operations that require the failed service. When the service recovers, clients reconnect/resynchronise through stable IDs/revisions rather than restarting with assumed fresh state.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Home data/state model
requirements.requirement: Home MUST maintain stable IDs/versioned records for installed packages/apps, Home services, Dashboard layouts/tiles, Mesh devices/pairings, notification records, search index records, permission/trust grants, account/session cache metadata and other Home-owned settings/control-plane entities. Display names, paths and UI ordering are not identity.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Home data/state model
requirements.requirement: Caches/indexes that are rebuildable MUST be marked as non-authoritative. Durable grants, package activation state, device trust and user layout/settings state MUST be recoverable and versioned. Home MUST distinguish device-local state from account/workspace-synchronised state explicitly.
requirements.applicability: Inherited platform/full Home contract; native-specific procedures require owning Team A evidence rather than assumed exemption.

requirements.heading: Home API
requirements.requirement: These are minimum canonical entry points. Every additional user-visible Home operation MUST have an equivalent supported API/domain action under the global API-parity rule. APIs MUST return structured state/errors and use stable IDs/revision checks for consequential or concurrent mutations.
